programs.title: Fiona Clark: Unafraid
programs.desc: In the 1970s, a young photographer caused a stir with her pictures of the queer scene in Auckland. Her work was censored, exhibitions were closed, and she herself faced social rejection. Despite this opposition, she continued her work, documenting marginalized communities and fighting for visibility and equality. A serious accident changed her life, but she remained true to her mission and became one of New Zealand's most important social documentary photographers.
